verses.1: And Itro, the priest from Midian, heard all that Moses had done for God and for his people, Israel. For Jehovah had brought Israel out of Egypt.
verses.2: And Yitro took Moses’ wife as a wife after his departure.
verses.3: And their two sons, one of whom was named Gerashom, because he said, “I was a foreigner in a foreign land.”
verses.4: And the name of the other one was Eliezer, because he was the god of my father. With his help, he saved me from the destruction of Pharaoh.
verses.5: And Itro’s son, Moses, and his sons, along with his wife, went to Moses to the sea, where he had built the Temple of God.
verses.6: And he said to Moses, “I will give you your wife and her two sons as gifts.”
verses.7: And Moses went out to read his commandment. He bowed down, kissed it, and asked his companion for forgiveness. Then they came forward.
verses.8: And Moses told his son everything that Jehovah had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt, regarding all the plagues that were sent upon them along their journey. It was Jehovah who caused these plagues to happen.
verses.9: And he praised all the good things that Jehovah had done for Israel, who saved them from Egypt.
verses.10: And Yitro said, “Blessed be Jehovah, who has saved you from the hands of Egypt and from the hands of Pharaoh, who has saved the people from the power of Egypt.”
verses.11: Now I know that Jehovah is greater than all the other gods, because He has done what He promised.
verses.12: And Terah took Moses’ son and offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and all the elders of Israel came together to eat bread with Moses’ son before God.
verses.13: And in the evening, Moses sat down to judge the people. The people stood before Moses from evening until morning.
verses.14: And Moses saw all that he did for the people. He said, “What is this that you do for the people? You sit alone, while all the people stand around you, from evening until morning.”
verses.15: And Moses said to his son, “When the people come to me to ask for God’s help.”
verses.16: For they had something to say to me, and I judged between one man and his neighbor. I knew the laws of God and His commandments.
verses.17: And Chothan Moses said to him, “It is not good what you are doing.”
verses.18: You and this people are also in trouble. It’s not possible for you to do this thing alone.
verses.19: Now, hear my advice. May God be with you. You shall be a people who stand before the Lord. You shall bring these words before the Lord.
verses.20: And you warned them about the laws and commandments. You showed them the path they should follow, as well as the actions that they must carry out.
verses.21: And you will see from all the people that those who are God-fearing, those who truly hate evil, have been put in charge of thousands of people. There are fifty thousand men who hold positions of authority, and twelve more who also hold important positions.
verses.22: And they will judge the people at every time. All great matters will be brought before you, and all minor matters will also be judged by them. They will then remove you from your position, and take you away.
verses.23: If you do this, and God commands you to do so, then you will be able to stand firm. And all this people will also come together at that place in peace.
verses.24: And Moses heard the voice of his Lord, and he did everything that was commanded him.
verses.25: Moses selected men from all of Israel. He appointed leaders for the people: there were thousands of chiefs, and also twenty thousand soldiers.
verses.26: And they would judge the people at every time, according to the difficult matters that came before Moses. They would also judge all minor matters themselves.
verses.27: And Moses sent out his successor, and he went to his own land.
